content:
The second annual Mercado Festival is coming to Laredo this weekend, bringing more than 100 vendors from Mexico to the Casa Blanca Event Center for three days of free binational culture, food, and live music.

The festival runs Friday, November 6, through Sunday, November 8, at the Casa Blanca Event Center, 5064 E. Saunders St., according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Admission is free. Vendors will sell artisan products, food, and crafts, with the State of Mexico as this year's featured state. Live music is part of the program, including mariachi on Friday and a tribute to Juan Gabriel on Saturday, according to the report.

The festival is organized by Webb County, led by Alberto Torres, executive director of the Webb County Fairgrounds and binational relations. County Judge Tano Tijerina and Precinct 1 Commissioner Jesse Gonzalez announced the event alongside Deputy Consul Martín Alcalá Salgado of the Mexican Consulate in Laredo, according to the report.

This year's festival moves to the Casa Blanca Event Center, a newly acquired Webb County venue, while the Webb County Fairgrounds pavilion remains under construction.

The first Mercado Festival took place in November 2025, featuring the state of Zacatecas.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “Mercado Festival returns to Laredo Nov. 6-8,” October 25, 2026.
